issues.title: b4w.ps1 fails on Linux due to CRLF line endings

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 help
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The PowerShell script should run on Linux when pwsh is installed.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: /usr/bin/env: 'pwsh\r': No such file or directory. The shebang line contains a carriage return, making the script unexecutable on Linux.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: b4w.ps1 has Windows-style CRLF line endings. On Linux, the kernel interprets the shebang as `pwsh\r` (with trailing carriage return) and cannot find an executable with that name. The file needs LF line endings.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: b4w.ps1 — needs `git add --renormalize` or `.gitattributes` entry to enforce LF line endings for .ps1 files, or convert to LF manually.
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add a `.gitattributes` rule: `b4w.ps1 text eol=lf` to force LF line endings on checkout
- Or convert b4w.ps1 to LF line endings in the repository
- The SKILL.md documentation correctly recommends b4w.sh for bash/Linux environments, which works around the issue
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: eval returns inconsistent results for the same page context

sections.body:
Run the same JavaScript eval twice on an Amazon search results page:
1. First eval: `document.querySelector('h2 a')` returns titles
2. Second eval: Same query returns empty strings for titles and URLs
Observed across four eval calls on the same page without navigation between them.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Repeated eval calls on the same page should return consistent results for the same DOM queries.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The first product extraction eval returned all four titles successfully. Subsequent eval calls (for URLs, reviews, combined extraction) returned empty strings for titles and URLs — even though price and rating data were still extracted. The last eval attempt returned titles in one run and empty strings in the next, suggesting non-deterministic behavior.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Unclear. Possible causes: (1) Amazon's page dynamically modifies the DOM between eval calls (A/B testing, lazy loading, ad injection). (2) The eval execution context differs between calls (iframe vs main frame). (3) A race condition where eval executes before the page fully stabilizes after the previous command. Further investigation needed.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add a `--wait-selector` flag to eval (mentioned in help) to ensure target elements are present before executing
- Document that eval may return partial results on dynamic pages and recommend htmlsnapshot for extraction
- Add built-in retry capability for eval when expected elements are missing
- Investigate whether each eval call shares the same execution context or creates a new one
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Accessibility tree snapshot output is overwhelmingly large for content-rich pages

sections.body: ./b4w.sh goto 'https://www.amazon.com/s?k=pens+to+draw+on+whiteboards' && ./b4w.sh snapshot -v 0 --stdout
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The snapshot should be scannable enough to find product elements without scrolling through thousands of lines.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The snapshot for Amazon search results was 70.7KB with 9 viewports. Even viewport 0 alone produced excessive output with deeply nested generic containers. Finding the search box ref (e232580) required scrolling through hundreds of lines of navigation and promotional content.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The accessibility tree preserves the full DOM hierarchy including all `generic` container divs. Amazon's page structure is deeply nested. The `snapshot -v 0` flag limits to one viewport but doesn't reduce nesting depth or filter non-interactive containers.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/snapshot.rs — snapshot rendering likely needs a mode to collapse deeply nested generic containers or filter to interactive elements only.
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add a `--depth` flag to limit tree depth in snapshot output
- Add a `--interactive-only` / `-i` mode that shows only elements with refs (interactive elements)
- Improve the default output by collapsing consecutive `generic` wrappers with no semantic role
- The existing `-i` mode exists but docs warn it strips generic divs which may hide product cards on e-commerce pages
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: htmlsnapshot inspect discovers navigation elements instead of page content

sections.body:
On Amazon search results page:
./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot
./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot inspect
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: htmlsnapshot inspect should discover product card selectors or at least identify the recurring product/search-result pattern.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The inspect command analyzed 20 of 3589 `<div>` matches but selected elements from the navigation assistant (`#nav-assist-search`, keyboard shortcuts) rather than product cards. Suggested selectors were all navigation-related (e.g., `span.shortcut-key.nav-assistant-card-font`).
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The inspect algorithm samples the first N elements from the DOM root (`:root`) without prioritizing elements in the main content area. On Amazon, navigation elements happen to be the first structurally similar siblings encountered. The tool lacks heuristics to prioritize main content over navigation/sidebar.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-rest — the htmlsnapshot inspect backend logic. Likely needs to prefer elements within `<main>` or with data attributes like `data-component-type`.
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Prioritize elements within `<main>` or `[role="main"]` for pattern discovery
- Weight elements with `data-component-type` or `data-asin` attributes higher
- Provide a `--selector` option to scope inspect to a specific container (e.g., `htmlsnapshot inspect --selector "[data-component-type='s-search-result']"`)
- The tip to use `htmlsnapshot summary` as an alternative was present in the output but is easy to miss in the noise
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Product review counts not extractable via htmlsnapshot or eval on Amazon

sections.body:
On Amazon search results:
1. ./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot get all text ".a-size-base.s-underline-text" --limit 10
2. ./b4w.sh eval --file get_reviews.js --json
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Review counts (e.g., '12,345') should be extractable via CSS selectors or JS eval.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: htmlsnapshot returned 'Visit the help section' and 'contact us' for the `.a-size-base.s-underline-text` selector. eval returned aria-label text '4.4 out of 5 stars, rating details' without the numeric review count. The actual review count (e.g., '12,345 ratings') was not captured by any extraction method attempted.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Amazon's review counts are likely rendered differently than expected — possibly in a separate span, loaded dynamically, or hidden in a non-standard attribute. The htmlsnapshot captures the static HTML after page load, which should include this data. The issue may be that Amazon's review count markup uses different classes than the selectors attempted.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Improve htmlsnapshot inspect to better detect rating/review patterns on e-commerce pages
- Add an Amazon-specific extraction recipe to htmlsnapshot-scenarios.md showing the correct selectors for review counts
- Consider adding a `--deep` flag to htmlsnapshot inspect that analyzes nested text patterns (e.g., '4.5 out of 5 stars' followed by a number)

issues.title: Two snapshot systems cause confusion for new users

sections.body: A new user reads the docs and tries to extract data. They encounter both 'snapshot' (accessibility tree) and 'htmlsnapshot' (HTML capture) and need to understand when to use each.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The distinction between the two snapshot systems should be clear from the first interaction, and the documentation should guide users to the right one without reading the full SKILL.md.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body:
The help output lists both `snapshot` and `htmlsnapshot` without explaining their relationship. The SKILL.md covers this in §4a (Choosing an Extraction Method) but a user who runs `./b4w.sh help` and skips the full documentation won't understand that:
- `snapshot` captures an accessibility tree with refs for interaction targeting
- `htmlsnapshot` captures static HTML for CSS selector extraction
- You need `snapshot` to get refs for clicking/filling, but `htmlsnapshot` to extract text with CSS selectors
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The CLI help compresses each command into one line, which is insufficient to explain the conceptual difference. The separation of concerns (accessibility tree for interaction, HTML for extraction) is an architectural decision that requires explanation.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli — the help text generator. The `snapshot` and `htmlsnapshot` sections in help output could cross-reference each other.
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add a brief cross-reference in the help output: 'snapshot — Capture accessibility tree for element refs. For CSS-based extraction, see htmlsnapshot.'
- Add a 'Quick Start' section to the top of `b4w.sh help` showing the most common command sequence
- Consider unifying the two systems under a single `snapshot` command with `--mode ax` and `--mode html` flags
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: SKILL.md documentation is comprehensive but overwhelming for first-time users

sections.body: Read skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md as a first-time user trying to complete a simple task (search Amazon, extract results).
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: A new user should be able to find the workflow for their task within the first screen of the documentation.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: SKILL.md is 508 lines covering 19 reference files, 7 decision trees, command maps, shell quoting, session management, tab management, and more. The 'Core Loop' (5 steps) and 'Copy-Paste Template' are at the top (great), but finding how to extract structured data from search results requires understanding the decision tree in §4a and then navigating to x-sql.md or htmlsnapshot.md.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The documentation is comprehensive and well-organized for reference, but lacks a task-oriented quick-start section that maps common tasks ('search Amazon', 'fill a form', 'take a screenshot') to exact command sequences.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add a 'Common Tasks' section with copy-paste recipes for the top 5-10 use cases (search + extract results, fill + submit form, take screenshot, crawl products)
- Add collapsible sections or a table of contents at the top
- Move reference material (shell quoting, tab management, PowerCSS) to a 'Deep Dive' section after the task-oriented content
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Short flag warning is noisy and confusing on Linux

sections.body: ./b4w.sh snapshot -v 0 --stdout
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Clean output without irrelevant warnings about PowerShell parameter binding.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body:
Every command using short flags like `-v` triggers:
⚠  Short flags detected: -v
   PowerShell may intercept these in other contexts (b4w.sh, direct pwsh).
   Prefer long-form equivalents: --output, --interactive, --viewport
   Or use b4w.sh / b4w.bat (cmd.exe) for full compatibility.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The warning logic in b4w.ps1 checks for short flags in the argument list before the CLI binary runs. It fires regardless of the shell environment — even when invoked through b4w.sh which already handles argument quoting correctly. The warning is irrelevant and misleading for Linux/bash users.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: b4w.ps1 — the $COMMON_INTERCEPTED check around line 39-47 should be suppressed when not running in an interactive PowerShell session (e.g., when invoked via b4w.sh).
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Suppress the short-flag warning when the script is invoked from a non-PowerShell parent (e.g., via b4w.sh)
- Or check if $env:PSExecutionPolicyPreference exists before emitting the warning
- Or simply remove the warning entirely since b4w.sh already handles argument quoting
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: No built-in command to detect or change Amazon delivery region

sections.body: Navigate to amazon.com — prices displayed in JPY. Try to find a command to detect or change the delivery region setting.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: There should be a way to see that the session's geolocation/delivery settings are affecting prices, and ideally a way to change them.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: All prices appeared in Japanese Yen (JPY) because the browser session had a Japan delivery address. There is no browser4-cli command to detect this, and no documentation about how delivery region affects Amazon search results. The user must infer this from the price currency symbols.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: This is a session state issue — the pre-existing browser session had cookies/localStorage from a previous Japan-region session. browser4-cli doesn't surface geolocation or region settings in its session management commands.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add a `session-info` command that surfaces region/locale/currency settings detected from the page
- Document in the 'Browser sessions' section how to clear session state to reset regional settings
- Add a `--fresh` flag to `goto` to bypass existing session state and start with a clean profile
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
